newsitem.title: UK: Zinc at 4-1/2 year high on LME, market active.
newsitem.headline: Zinc at 4-1/2 year high on LME, market active.

text.p: Zinc prices raced to the highest levels for nearly 4-1/2 years on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Monday, resuming a strong bull-trend, traders said.
Three months prices were indicated at $1,240/1,242 at one stage in late afternoon trade, up from Friday's $1,218 close.
Traders said the market has been building up for this move, following a recent period of consolidation when prices settled back under $1,200 a tonne at one stage.

The trend on Monday was assisted by patterns elsewhere in the base metals complex, where copper was at a nine-month high, aluminium reached a one-year peak, and nickel climbed to its best for 9-1/2 months.
Speculators have been buying as well, investment fund interest has washed through the metal market on several occasions recently.

Additionally, the fundamental picture is constructive, with stocks falling consistently. LME inventories presently stand at 470,650 tonnes, down from 506,825 tonnes at the end of 1996. --Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
